source_text: Deinde etiamsi hoc solum ad carnem referas, nec sic potest haec intellegentiae tuae fatuitas excusari, qua dicis: Omnes ille unus fuerunt, cum eo tempore, quo peccavit Adam, iam duo essent homines, non unus, id est ipse et uxor eius, de quorum substantia, non culpa genus hominum, secundum quod Deus instituerat, pullulavit.
pass_a_gloss: Next even if you refer this only to the flesh, not even so can this foolishness of your understanding be excused, by which you say: All that one were, when at that time in which Adam sinned there were already two human beings, not one, that is himself and his wife, from whose substance, not guilt, the race of human beings, according to what God had instituted, sprouted.
pass_b_english: Moreover, even if you refer this only to flesh, the stupidity of your understanding still cannot be excused. You say, ‘All were that one man,’ although at the time Adam sinned there were already two human beings, not one: himself and his wife. From their substance, not their fault, the human race sprouted according to God’s institution.

choices.why: Julian's pair with iustitia: guilt as culpable will, not a nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
